summary: OpenAI's Greg Brockman describes the company's internal AI-driven cybersecurity defense strategy and issues recommendations for other organizations to adopt agentic AI tools for security triage and remediation.

mechanisms.reason: OpenAI states that nearly all of its initial security alerts are now triaged by AI before humans are involved, describing a real internal shift of work from analysts to agents.
mechanisms.quote: Today, almost all of our initial security alerts are triaged by intelligence before humans are looped in.

practices.reason: The staged autonomy plan for security agents (read-only scan, advisory PR review, live triage, automated closure) is a pipeline design an engineering team could copy, but no gain figures are given.
practices.quote: Start by running a read-only security scan against one repository, or have an agent review previously resolved alerts using read-only access to your existing logs. Let it summarize evidence and recommend a disposition while a human makes every decision. As confidence grows, move to advisory pull-request scanning, then live alert triage, then automatic closure of narrowly defined false positives.

practices.reason: Guidance to prioritize security assessments against specific system classes is a measurement practice an engineer could adopt, though it is generic and unquantified.
practices.quote: Prioritize assessments against internet-facing services, authentication flows, infrastructure as code, deployment pipelines, and systems handling sensitive information first.
